question:
I am handing over a finished system to a client whose in-house team will keep developing it after delivery. Besides the program itself, what written material should I prepare for the client, for its end users and for my own organization, and for how long should it be retained?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:
# Summary

When handing over a finished system, software engineers must prepare documentation for the client (including functional specs, design, test suites, and operating environment details), for end users (safe/unsafe use, warnings, sensitive-data protection), and for their own organization (requirements specs, design docs, tools, test specs, problems encountered). Documents should be retained [SWEBOK excerpt 412e1c8b2cdb4ad2a682] as required by organizational or regulatory rules.

# Guidelines

- Provide documentation of functional specifications, [SWEBOK excerpt 1cede21b94389e988d7e] when the client will acquire ownership of or the right to modify the source code. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Professional Practice and Collaboration in Software Engineering/Professional Responsibility and Intellectual Property in Software Engineering/Documentation and Requirements Trade-off Management/Documentation Standards and Requirements for Software Engineers.md)

- For the development organization, supply [SWEBOK excerpt a2d00dbb452e0cce9e9d] tools used, software test specifications and results, details about adopted software engineering methods, and problems encountered during development. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Professional Practice and Collaboration in Software Engineering/Professional Responsibility and Intellectual Property in Software Engineering/Documentation and Requirements Trade-off Management/Documentation Standards and Requirements for Software Engineers.md)

- For external stakeholders (customers and users), provide [SWEBOK excerpt 7a8cf64cb6874668904d] their needs, descriptions of safe and unsafe use, explanations of how to protect sensitive information, and clear identification of warnings and critical procedures. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Professional Practice and Collaboration in Software Engineering/Professional Responsibility and Intellectual Property in Software Engineering/Documentation and Requirements Trade-off Management/Documentation Standards and Requirements for Software Engineers.md)

- Document [SWEBOK excerpt 152611cb851250127f97], and relevant information pertaining to attribute, license type, and sourcing. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Professional Practice and Collaboration in Software Engineering/Professional Responsibility and Intellectual Property in Software Engineering/Documentation and Requirements Trade-off Management/Documentation Standards and Requirements for Software Engineers.md)

- [SWEBOK excerpt 3195bf83cb2eca8378f7]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Professional Practice and Collaboration in Software Engineering/Professional Responsibility and Intellectual Property in Software Engineering/Documentation and Requirements Trade-off Management/Documentation Standards and Requirements for Software Engineers.md)

- Release notes describing new capabilities, known problems, and platform requirements, along with installation or upgrade instructions, should be included in the release package delivered to the client. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Processes/Release Management Tools and Documentation Requirements.md)

- [SWEBOK excerpt e2b929f7b6c130d7557c] should be captured in a version description document (VDD). (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Processes/Software Release Management and Deployment Processes.md)

- Record and document design rationale—[SWEBOK excerpt bf3e253b4433925b4521] enhance long-term maintainability for those who will modify or maintain the system after delivery. - Prepare a software maintenance plan specifying [SWEBOK excerpt c3f9b85a22b5819ebd7b]; [SWEBOK excerpt e109f711e9285a8adf5f]. - Develop a concept of operations (CONOPS) or operations plan that specifies [SWEBOK excerpt 72ef32741fe64ab7ef27] is operational. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Software Engineering Operations Planning and CONOPS Development.md)

- Keep [SWEBOK excerpt fc35f1fae863dd061b6f], and delegate [SWEBOK excerpt e576b0ffe2ef18fcca69]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Software Maintenance Management and Organization/Organizing Software Maintenance Responsibilities/Developer vs. Separate Maintenance Team Trade-offs.md)

- Software items that should be placed under configuration control—and thus formally handed over—[SWEBOK excerpt ddc65334e6acdac03cc1]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management and Change Control/Software Configuration Items Selection and Change Recording.md)

- Outputs of the build process [SWEBOK excerpt a4ef685722d26ada8f79] and should be retained for future reference. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Processes/Build Quality Assurance and Configuration Management/Build Process Quality Verification and Documentation.md)

- After project closure, [SWEBOK excerpt 3d7d83a03042e57ec27e] [SWEBOK excerpt a7a3c6c662d95103fd5c]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Quality Management and Project Oversight/Software Measurement and Organizational Learning/Project Closure and Archival Procedures.md)

- At closure, document relevant stakeholders' acceptance and record any known problems. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Quality Management and Project Oversight/Software Measurement and Organizational Learning/Project Closure and Archival Procedures.md)

- Update the organization's measurement database with relevant project data and capture lessons learned for organizational learning and improvement. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Quality Management and Project Oversight/Software Measurement and Organizational Learning/Software Engineering Measurement and Organizational Learning.md)

- Written software engineering products—including source code, project plans, requirements documents, risk analyses, design documents, test plans, and user manuals—[SWEBOK excerpt 71f0e1e15453ebcfae33]. - Requirements documentation should be maintained throughout the software's service life to capture and communicate intent for engineers who maintain the code but may not have been its original authors.
